finding: CSV BOM assertion precedes content validation on 5 direct-table CSVs
boundary: All CSV entries must start with UTF-8 BOM; empty files (0 data rows + header) correctly assert header presence
verdict: PASS — BOM check isolated early, header extraction via split() expected to always yield ≥1 element (header line)

finding: IDOR scoping on journal_entry_lines.csv via JOIN parsing
path: Parse CSV header → locate entry_id column → iterate data rows → HashSet lookup of allowed_entry_ids
boundary: If CSV is empty (0 data rows): for-loop doesn't execute, jel_data_count=0 ✓. If CSV leaks company_B rows: HashSet.contains() fails assertion ✓
verdict: PASS — metadata.rowCount corroborates CSV data count (assert_eq! catches mismatch)

finding: CSV parser assumes header + data both use semicolon delimiter; malformed header (different delimiter) not caught
path: cols = header.split(';').collect() → position() on cols[cid_pos]; if header has ',' then position() finds wrong column
boundary: Edge: header='company_id;X;Y' but data row='X,Z,W' → parser splits data on ';' → cid_pos out-of-bounds panic
verdict: ACCEPTABLE — spec mandates ';' delimiter (AC #29 CSV format); malformed header is app-level bug (not test responsibility)

finding: Audit poll loop waits 2s (20 × 100ms) for async best-effort insert
path: for _ in 0..20: fetch_optional(WHERE user_id=? AND action='exports.global') → sleep 100ms if None
boundary: If audit insert latency > 2s: loop exhausts, row=None, .expect() panics with diagnostic message ✓
verdict: PASS — failure mode is explicit panic with clear error msg; no silent pass
risk: flakiness if CI latency > 2s, but message documents intent

finding: Audit filtering uses user_id (FK isolation), not company_id (audit_log schema has no company_id column)
path: Query: WHERE user_id=? AND action='exports.global' → no company_id filter (FK users.company_id guarantees isolation)
boundary: Multi-tenant safety: each user belongs to exactly 1 company; filtering by user_id is sufficient ✓
verdict: PASS — design correct per Pass 3 ECH review (C1 ground-truth validation of audit_log schema)

finding: details_json field decoded as serde_json::Value (JSON BLOB type), not Option<String>
path: sqlx::query_as::<_, (..., serde_json::Value)> with details_json parameter; deserializes JSON directly
boundary: If details_json is NULL: serde_json::Value::Null ✓; if malformed JSON: query fails at deserialize step (caught by .unwrap())
verdict: PASS — type signature enforces JSON deserialization; no string-parsing fallback risk

finding: Invoice lines JOIN scoping assertion non-tautological: 1 invoice_line inserted per company (A & B)
path: invoices::list_all_lines_by_company(pool, a.company_id) → JOIN invoices ON invoice_lines.invoice_id=invoices.id WHERE invoices.company_id=?
boundary: If JOIN omits WHERE invoices.company_id filter: result=2 (both A & B rows) → assertion fails (expected 1) ✓ CATCHES REGRESSION
verdict: PASS — assertion count (1 vs 2) proves JOIN scoping; not tautological (≠ empty result both ways)

finding: Date suffix extraction uses hardcoded char positions: fname[fname.len()-14..fname.len()-4] for '-YYYY-MM-DD'
boundary: Edge: filename='kesh-export-ABC-2026-01-01.zip' (28 chars) → [14..24]='ABC-2026-01'; count dashes=2 ✓. But if company slug variable length (vs fixed 'ABC'), boundaries might shift
verdict: ACCEPTABLE — spec says pattern 'kesh-export-.+-YYYY-MM-DD.zip'; regex-like validation would be more robust, but hardcoded extraction works if slug is non-empty

finding: Details JSON assertions check specific fields: company_id, byte_size, csv_count, fiscal_year_scope, duration_ms
path: details["company_id"].as_i64().unwrap() → assert matches ctx.company_id; similar for byte_size (u64>0), csv_count (16), fiscal_year_scope (string), duration_ms (number)
boundary: If field missing: .unwrap() panics; if type mismatch (e.g., csv_count is string not u64): as_u64()=None → .unwrap() panics ✓
